Dawson Management

Dawson Partners, a leader in alternative asset management, delivers innovative private market solutions. 

I designed a new end-to-end flow for customizable dashboards using a component library and drag-and-drop interface, enabling partners to create personalized analytics for their teams.

View Site

Future-proofing dashboards

With no product, they needed a user flow to showcase interactive layouts. The goal was to design a professional, modular platform that was easy to use, rebranding away from legacy competitor designs.

The vision was to create a new experience for building scalable, modular components that meet the needs of any analytics team while remaining simple and innovative.

Customizing effortlessly

Gone are the days of static layouts; now, components can be easily edited and rearranged with intuitive interactions. Users can quickly adjust their dashboards without technical skills, saving time and streamlining workflows.

Enhanced team analytics

Dynamic dashboards can now be created using templates that are shareable and customizable, enhancing functionality and fostering collaboration across teams.

Configuring for flexibility

Dynamic dashboards now offer complete configurability of components, moving beyond static metrics and charts to create an adaptable experience that empowers more insightful decision-making.

Optimizing for collaboration

Annotations are now faster than ever, enabling users to mark up documents and organize labels with ease. Teams can stay efficient by reviewing annotations twice as fast.

pages.title: Copilot 内容生态 | Jiazhao Xu
pages.text:
许嘉昭 Jiazhao Xu
EN
中
Copilot 内容生态

为AI设计端到端内容体验

Copilot 内容生态是我对微软获取内容并分发这一流程所涉及的产品的统称，内容指C端用户日常阅读、观看的文章、视频、播客、图集等。

微软内容生态每天与超过 20,000 家全球媒体与机构合作，提供多语种、多领域的新闻、财经、体育与生活资讯。这些内容通过微软的全球分发体系，整合至 Windows、Copilot、Bing、MSN 与 Edge 新标签页等用户端产品中,为数亿用户提供个性化的信息体验。我同时负责用户端和媒体机构端的设计工作，涵盖内容供给和分发两个环节。

微软内容的供给和分发路径

若想尝试体验微软的内容服务，你可以打开 Edge浏览器的新Tab页面（下方左图为Copilot Discover灰度版，您可能需要被灰到才能看到此版本），或者直接打开msn.com

Edge新标签页与MSN

C端内容分发与体验体系

当优质内容接入微软生态后，我们通过不同的终端产品将其智能分发给用户。

我负责 Copilot 中新闻、财经与天气的体验设计，重点在于如何平衡“AI 对话体验”与“内容浏览体验”两种模式的融合。

在设计过程中，我主要解决了以下挑战：

信息结构整合：在新闻、股票、天气等模块中，通过一致的组件体系和视觉语言，形成多模态的内容呈现体验。
AI 对话与内容融合：针对用户在 Copilot 中的对话与生成任务，探索 AI 如何辅助内容阅读、总结与延展。
设计系统延展：作为业务设计师，频繁地和总部沟通，对齐最新的用户体验，并在必要时凝练自身业务的产出来反哺Copilot基础体验和设计系统。

天气、新闻、财经等内容设计

🎨

在设计Copilot时，很多时候要思考到底如何平衡对话和内容展示两部分，通常来讲，用户来到Copilot的使用场景更贴近于传统AI工具（如ChatGPT、豆包等），但同行业内其他竞争者一样，微软在尝试给AI带来更多场景，希望用户来到Copilot的目的不只是生成文章、翻译文段等任务，也希望用户来体验其他不同功能。（目前Copilot中有Lab功能，其中包含大量非对话功能）

独立股票信息页面

我同时负责 MSN 财经产品的设计。相比 Copilot，MSN 页面的信息密度更高，布局也更紧凑。这种差异源于两个产品的用户心理：Copilot 用户多为随意浏览内容、偶尔查看股票；MSN 财经则面向准专业用户，信息完整性优先于舒适的阅读体验。

Copilot 与 MSN 对比

欢迎体验Copilot：https://copilot.microsoft.com/

B端内容平台与合作生态：MSN Partner Hub

在内容供应端，微软通过MSN Partner Hub为全球内容合作伙伴（如 CNN、BBC 等）提供统一的创作与数据管理平台。

我负责该平台的全部设计工作，包括信息架构、设计系统与数据体验，平台为合作伙伴提供包括：

内容同步与编辑工具
数据表现与流量分析
粉丝增长与收益监控
账户与品牌管理

MSN Partner Hub 首页

🔒

因数据合规问题，我无法提供更多页面截图

同时我还在尝试引入 AI 辅助创作功能（如 AI 助手与内容优化工具），帮助合作伙伴提升内容生产与表现质量。

保密项目

💡

在该项目中，我们特别关注 AI 内容的版权与幻觉风险控制，确保依托 AI 的同时不影响合作方利益与内容真实性。

我负责维护该平台的设计系统，与前端团队协作，确保设计还原度和视觉一致性。近期，我主导了平台的视觉系统升级：

👀

​

Hey, my name is koko!

To give you a brief introduction to myself. I currently live in Shanghai and I have worked as a designer for over 11 years. I graduated from Southeast University with a Bachelor's Degree in Industrial Design in 2012 and a Master's Degree in Art Design in 2015.

 

At that time, like most designers, I was not getting properly trained at school of becoming an experience designer or product designer. Most of my experience comes from my industry practice during my career. 

​

So after graduation, I started off my career as a visual designer with Tencent Technology, I was in that position for four years and was promoted to the senior visual designer. Then I am looking for a  role that is both strategic and hands-on in terms of design. Luckily I had the opportunity to join Frog Design. Working at a consultancy my role is extremely versatile. Although my role is senior visual designer, my actual role is kind of an experience designer. During my career at Frog, I have been working in a variety of industries, and digital transformation projects.

​

In 2021, I left Frog and joined Zilliz (Creator of Milvus, the world’s leading open-source vector database) as Design Manager, leading a team of Product and Visual Designers. I oversee all creative & digital design work for Zilliz’s brand image and digital products. I lead and mentor design teams, with the versatility to engage in hands-on work when needed

KEY EXPERTISE

Empathy-driven, user-centric approach leveraging Design Thinking

Global UI/UX craftsmanship enhanced by AI tool

Technical understanding and practical experience with LLMs and AI-driven products

Branding & Visual communication

Storytelling & Design Mentorship

Design System / UI Kit / Visual Guideline

EXPERIENCE

DEGREE & EDUCATION

TEACHING / SPEAKING ENGAGEMENT

Got a project?
Learn how I work↗
WHAT CAN I SAY MORE?
Personally, I’m a self-driven designer and always willing to go above and beyond in my role to deliver excellent results. I always get excited when starting a new project because I know I have the opportunity to get out of my comfort zone and expand my skill sets. 

As both a designer and manager, I enjoy constantly deepening my knowledge of the world and humanity through design and communication. I‘m a forever learner and will constantly cultivate design craft and strategy.

Design is a mindset - not tied to a specific role, yet many enterprises and even designers haven't realized this. Once you embrace it, you can't stop thinking about how things could be better - design, management, or utilizing AI. I share my thoughts on Rednote, Medium and Linkedin, aiming to build a continuous growth cycle: question, act, reflect and improve.
Designing for products means making decisions from industry and contextual perspective. We're not talking about beauty, we're talking about whether it works, whether it's really needed by people and whether it can help companies survive or grow as well. I think it is very challenging to answer these questions.

I've done a lot of live projects, so I'm very familiar with iterative design, design sprints, and collaborating with engineers. For complex products, I tend to build the design system and set principles from the beginning.

I am passionate about helping companies to achieve their goals via human-centered design. And I believe that design thinking and behavior science could go together and should go together.
WHEN WORK IS A PLEASURE, LIFE IS A JOY!
In my free time, I enjoy the fun and energy that life brings to us. I love pop songs, especially the old ones, and I have a collection of Beatles, Heavy Metal and Chinese Rock on vinyl. I have two very long-haired cats🐱. I like to hang out with my friends at park🌳 and cafes☕️.Here are some pictures of me taken by my friends❤️ and myself☺️.

Less is more. Keeping things clear wherever I can, even when it seems impossible.
According to Maslow's theory and behavioral science, human needs and decisions ultimately follow emotions, and we design for emotions.

ABOUT ME

I'm a product designer based in the Greater Seattle Area with front-end chops, who loves to design and prototype simple and meaningful experiences that improve people's lives. I am drawn to designing for physical experiences, and my design superpower is using systems-thinking to connect the dots between features or products, while staying focused on the details. I’ve enjoyed working in several domains over the years: trust and safety in multi-sided platforms, and behavior change through habit design and data visualization.

I started designing in high school and never stopped. My education background is in HCI and Media Arts, with a former research interest in behavior change and data visualization. I've also hacked Nintendo Wiimotes, built apps for the Microsoft Surface, and prototyped hardware with the Arduino (check out my audio visualizer and semi-viral Super Mario Bros on an 8x8 LED matrix). When not designing, I'm photographing people, crocheting cute things, tending to my 60 pandemic plants, escaping all the rooms (see below), and learning another instrument or language. I'm unabashedly addicted to claw machines and boba.

pages.text:
Deepak Mallya
Featured All Work About Resumé Press
A problem-solver, lateral thinker and maker, my work predominantly explores how we interact with technology. I enjoy working with people across disciplines, allowing me to learn and apply interdisciplinary approaches to tackling complex challenges. 
I believe in taking innovation outside the lab. 
I am currently an Interaction Designer at Google, working on AI on Personal Devices across Deepmind and Android. 
While pursuing my masters I co-founded, The Tyre Collective. Where we invented a device that helps capture tyre wear emissions—the second largest microplastic pollutant in our environment. We are now partnering with some of the largest auto and tyre manufacturers to see our devices on cars.  
Previously, I co-founded and lead product design at Treemouse—an award winning strategy and research consultancy in India. I helped build the Treemouse, team, culture and client base. 
My work has won various international recognition from Fast Company, The James Dyson Foundation, The Mayor of London, and Core77 and have been featured on the BBC, Reuters, Forbes, The Guardian, Sky News, The Times and The Evening Standard. They have also been exhibited in institutions like The Saatchi Gallery, CES, Imperial College, London Design Biennale amongst others.

Design
is Funny®
©2026
Funny® is the design work of Daniele 
*
Buffa, roman designer, now based in London, UK. Currently Staff Product Designer @ 
Spotify
.

With 10 years of experience in the design industry, I have had the opportunity to work with both industry leaders like Google, Sony, Headspace and more, and also up and coming startups.

I have been fortunate to have my work recognised with awards such as a Cannes Lion, D&AD Pencil, CSSDA, FWA and Awwwards Site of the Day.



I am also a judge at Awwwards, and have created courses on UI & Motion Design on Awwwards, Dribbble, and soon also on Domestika. I am passionate about pushing the boundaries of Design, and breaking the rules when needed.

*

Buffa ( ˈ boo-f:ah) from the Italian means funny, comic, droll.

Background

Ever since I can remember, I've always been drawn to creating and sharing my creations with others. While I can't say for certain if I had a natural talent for it, I found immense joy in seeing people appreciate the things I made.

When I first discovered UX design in 2017, it felt like a perfect blend of two worlds I was deeply interested in and naturally inclined towards: technology and art. The moment I realized the potential of this field, I dove in headfirst, never looking back.

Now, I'm designing products, hoping they can bring impact and values to the people around the world.

About
Résumé
IBM Research Almaden Genomics

 

Almaden Genomics is a science product group from IBM Research, with the vision to expedite current genetic engineering process through product. The team aims to convert current engineering heavy gnome pipeline process into a no-code workflow builder. That not only allows less technically advanced researchers to participate in pipeline building, but also leverage tech to bring more efficiency to the process for others in the field. My design team and I play a crucial role in our project to transform the gnome pipeline building experience.

Project

Duration: 11 months
Role: Sr UX Designer
I worked with Bioinformaticians, Clients, PM, Engineers, Visual Designer
Problem Area: Bioinformatics Workflow

Key Insights 

Out of the initial user groups we researched, besides technical limitations being the biggest constraint in genomics pipeline building. Here are some other areas where users get frustrated during the process:

Tedious file organization prep before building

Continuously test pipeline to meet expected behavior

Troubleshoot for errors

Now, we understand the pain points across different user groups, that we could help address on the user experience end. However, we need to first establish an information architecture that allows users to navigate smoothly while satisfying their building process. 

Our team came together in Mural, using card to represent each information piece we need in the product. Out of 4 different information structures we sketched out to explore different possibilities of navigations, and received feedback from our cross-functional teams. This is the one that our entire team felt most confident moving forward with. 

We did a decomposition of the information architecture, and summarized the screens we need in our product. Then we brainstormed via sketching for each of them. We diverged to sketch out as many options as we could on our own, and we converged back to critique and vote on the option we want to move forward with.

Design. Develop. Gym. Sleep. Repeat.

That's all I do.

Master's in digital design
HvA
2025 – 2026

I studied Mechatronics Engineering at the Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta. In my second year I tried to become an Android developer. Spent a month just getting Android Studio to install, then a full year stuck in the tutorial loop without shipping a single app. When a friend asked me to build something and I couldn't deliver, I knew that path wasn't working.

I needed income, so I started making whiteboard animation videos on Fiverr. My first gig paid ₦2,920 (about $8). But while learning to make those videos, I installed Illustrator and Photoshop again, and my old love for graphics came back hard. A designer at my school, JayKay, was doing incredible work. Through him I discovered that people designed products for a living. That was the moment everything clicked. I wrote about the full story here.

That was about six years ago. Since then I've designed and shipped products across fintech, healthcare, logistics, and developer tools. I was the founding designer at SIPP (helped them get into Techstars in 2024) and PHPSandbox. Senior product designer at Figo. I worked on cross-border payments at Changera back in 2019, before the space got crowded. I also helped Bonadocs and Changera secure grants and funding, over $200K between them.

The funny thing is, I write production code now. React, Next.js, TypeScript. The same guy who couldn't get Android Studio running. I can prototype in Figma in the morning and have it running in the browser by afternoon. Developers don't have to redo my interfaces because I already built them to their constraints. It's not a party trick. It just makes everything faster.

I mentor designers on the side. A few of them have landed their first industry roles, and honestly that keeps me going more than most project launches do.

I recently finished a Master's in Digital Design at Hogeschool van Amsterdam, which was equal parts humbling and energizing.

I take pictures too. If I ever pull my camera out to take yours, just know, that's my way of telling you you're beautiful.

pages.text:
Skip to Main Content
Sunny Kim

Work

About

Resume

Writing on a moving page
How we brought handwriting to life on reflowable text and made it feel natural on Kindle Scribe.
Role
Lead designer
Product
Kindle Scribe
Areas
Strategy, Design
Launch
Dec 2024
View live site
Background

When Kindle Scribe launched in November 2022, it included two main note-taking features: "Sticky notes", which allowed users to attach handwritten or typed notes to specific words in reflowable books, and "Notebooks", a separate space for free-form drawing and writing.

However, customers couldn’t write directly on the pages of reflowable books—something many expected from a stylus-enabled device.

 

This was due to technical limitations with how the system handled page history (backstack), which prevented on-page annotations. Freeform writing was only supported on static formats like PDFs. While users appreciated the large screen and flexible notebook tools, they consistently voiced frustration over the inability to annotate directly on book text, revealing a key gap in the reading and writing experience.

Existing annotation experience on Scribe. All notes were contained within a sticky note that was anchored on a book text. 

Why can't we just write on the book?

One of the core technical challenges in designing annotation experiences on E-readers is the dynamic nature of reflowable text. Unlike static page formats, reflowable content adjusts to user preferences such as font size, margin width, and device orientation. While this flexibility is a key benefit for reading, it introduces significant complexity for anchoring user-created notes.

 

For annotations to remain meaningful and revisitable, they must stay tethered to the specific content they reference; even as that content shifts position due to reflow. This required us to design an interaction model and system architecture that could preserve the logical anchor of each note in a fluid text environment, ensuring consistency and reliability without compromising the reading experience.

While writing directly on page could work initially, these notes starts losing their context as soon as the text reflows. 

Approach

To address the challenges of fluid content and constrained writing surfaces in reflowable books, we introduced a three-part annotation experience that balances flexibility with structure.

 

First, we enabled structured annotations; allowing users to highlight, underline, and outline directly on the text using a stylus, with each hand-drawn stroke automatically cleaned up into structured, consistent markings to preserve readability. Second, we designed an active canvas interaction, letting users insert writable space between lines or paragraphs by tap-and-hold with the stylus; the canvas is dynamically anchored and sized, offering a natural and responsive way to write inline without disrupting content flow. Finally, we added a side panel that can be activated with a tap to expand the book’s margin. This provides a dedicated space for notetaking and reviewing, integrating both handwritten annotations and reimagined stickynotes into a single, scannable context.

 

Together, these solutions respect the flexibility of reflowable content while giving users more control and visibility over their annotations.

We started designing by defining the types of annotations users can create inside a book.

Readers can underline, highlight, circle text selections, which will get structured and saved to their Annotations notebook.

Once readers start writing anywhere on the page, an active canvas will appear as an overlay on top of the book text. It will then get inserted into the page.

Readers can open the side panel to take notes in the margin space and see existing sticky notes 

Active canvas notes are available to view on mobile devices.

Active canvas notes are available to view on mobile devices.

Impact

The post-launch experience drove meaningful impact on both product quality and customer satisfaction—reflected in a higher star rating (from 4.1 to 4.3), increased monthly active users, and a noticeable rise in in-book annotation engagement.

About Me

Hello!
I'm Yobi.

I’m a UX Designer at Google based in California, currently leading the Watch Ads experience on YouTube. Previously, I led UX across Shorts, Creator, SMB, and Youth experiences, shaping how diverse audiences create, connect, and thrive on the platform. Before Google, I led design teams at NETGEAR and partnered with startups to build successful product experiences.

​

 

My background in architecture, along with recognition as one of Lighting Magazine’s “40 Under 40” designers, has deeply influenced how I approach design, balancing structure with creativity, vision with execution, and user needs with business outcomes. This foundation has trained me to think systemically, move fluidly between strategy and craft, and bring clarity to ambiguity.

​

 

Beyond my core role, I'm exploring how AI is reshaping design practice from creative judgment to how designers collaborate with intelligent systems. About

Precious Payload is an online marketplace and an expert team that help new space companies execute their missions fast and reliably. Launching a scientific project? Delivering commercial cargo? Running in-orbit experiments? We've got you covered.

My journey

I joined the team as a design consultant and shortly moved in-house to support the team on their great mission as a designer and a product owner.

Learning new space

The team has done a great work in figuring out product market fit. My main focus is the digital part of the business. My role is to tie business development and digital, and streamline both sides — client facing product and internal infrastructure.



Space is quite small industry. Along with learning the new domain and digging through details of space launches specifics, I had to adjust my approach to qualitative and quantitative research.


During my work there we’ve improved marketing and onboarding conversions, and re-vamped internal systems. I’ve also enhanced team processes: product analytics, design and delivery.

Projects
Design System

While implementing a design system, it's important to keep in mind the current business needs. Comprehensive guidelines would be overkill for a small, rapid team. However, some foundations were laid down to boost consistency, speed, and quality of delivery.

Landing page

A challenge of explaining the value of the product that didn't exist on the market before.

Launch schedule

The world's most comprehensive list of satellite launch opportunities. A unique database maintained by the team that let satellite developers find their next best launch.

Hi! I'm Jacqueline Guo — a product designer ⚙︎, percussionist ♪, and senior studying Computer Science + Game Design @USC ✌︎.

RECENTLY ↓

Human Interface Design Intern
Developer Experience Design Team, working on Xcode

THE TL;DR

Helping people do their life's best work.

I'm excited about working on complex, technical products with a high bar for craft that make a positive impact on our world. 

I'm also passionate about creative and developer tools and building community through in-person events.

MY DESIGN STRENGTHS

Solving difficult, deeply technical problems

I lean into complex design and visionary product problems, particularly in technical domains. Diving into code, prototyping with LLMs, cross-referencing existing patterns from other products, and extensively documenting decisions are a regular part of my design process.

Creating polished work across design disciplines

Before I knew product design existed, I was a graphic designer and spent a lot of time dabbling in adjacent disciplines like illustration and animation, which taught me the foundations of designing beautiful interfaces and are spaces I still love to work in today.

Staying curious and tuned into the tech world

I stay curious and up-to-date with what's going on in tech (via Twitter, podcasts, etc. and document it on Are.na). I'm always trying and learning about new products, because I believe it is part of the job to understand the vast landscape we are building software in.

OUTSIDE OF DESIGN

I was a musician in a past life

Before design, I wanted to be a professional percussionist. It was here where I first learned how to dream big and work hard to make those dreams a reality. I'm currently drumming with the USC Marching Band, and have performed at the finale screening of Severance Season 2 at the 2025 Paleyfest as well as with The Rose at Coachella, among other gigs. Previously, I was a member of the SFSYO and toured Europe with the 2022 NYO-USA.

I fill my free time with…

Catching up with my friends, more design (personal projects like designing fonts), playing games (mahjong, Monument Valley, and Stardew Valley are a few favorites), journaling, watching football highlights, and endlessly curating my Spotify playlists.

REFLECTIONS

A Summer at Apple

This past summer, I was a Human Interface Design Intern at Apple working on Developer Experience in Xcode. During my internship, I dove into the world of designing professional creative and developer tools, understanding underlying technical constraints and the structure of Xcode projects, what it's like to deploy apps on an Apple platform, as well as how AI is changing how people create and evolve software over time.

I was lucky to get to work on a problem I had encountered myself while using Xcode, spending weeks experimenting on the platform and mocking up ideas. What started as a project exploring small but mighty UI changes evolved into laying out a product vision for the future of building on the IDE.

In the end, I had the opportunity to present high-fidelity screens that reimagined a foundational workflow to my VP! I also got to develop an idea for iContest, Apple's internal intern competition with my friend Anna. I'm especially grateful for my team for being incredible mentors, both in design and in life, the fellow interns in my office, and the many wonderful people I met across the company who were willing to take the time to chat with me. You all made this summer incredibly special!

pages.text:
Andy Li, 20

Junior at NYU

Computer Science Major

New York City

Andy is a junior studying CS at NYU. He spends his semester working hard on his class projects and assignments during the week, and he enjoys his weekends by going to EDM concerts or learning how to DJ, as he aspires to become a rising DJ. With a DJ controller, he noticed that his DJ software allows for a few music platforms to be integrated into the app. The one he knows most is SoundCloud, as he used to listen to mixtapes in high school through there. He hopes that his familiar experience with SoundCloud will help him level up his music knowledge and DJ aspirations.

Needs

Pain Points




Andy is disappointed with SoundCloud's limited personalized experience. The absence of personalized features like a collaborative playlist with friends and friend’s music activity makes competitors the preferred music platform.

Andy faces challenges in using SoundCloud for DJing due to a lack of guidance. The platform falls short in supporting tasks such as playlist transfers, finding songs with similar BPM, and overall streamlining the experience for artists.

Andy struggles to discover remixes on SoundCloud. The platform's openness to new artists publishing music creates a cluttered search experience with less accurate results and potentially lower quality songs.

Emotional State with SoundCloud

Content

Satisfaction

Engagement


Andy needs a more efficient method to discover music tailored to his EDM/Pop preferences, making the exploration process smoother and more enjoyable.
Aspiring to become a DJ, Andy requires support and guidance within SoundCloud, especially when using it for DJ software integration. This includes seamless playlist transfers, assistance in finding songs with matching BPM, and overall better support for artists using SoundCloud as their primary platform.

I wanted to create a user persona to embody the ideal SoundCloud user based on the full research process I conducted, incorporating insights from user interviews, competitor analysis, and instances of poor experiences. By synthesizing the gathered data, my aim is to represent the user's preferences, pain points, and behaviors, allowing for a more focused and effective redesign for our ideal user.

Major Redesigns

IDEATION




I implemented a button enabling users to switch between light and dark modes based on their preferences.




I introduced a left column for easy access to all playlists and liked songs.




The center displayed the SoundCloud Feed, often overlooked by users but serving as a valuable tool for discovering new music.




Below the feed, a section was created for recently played playlists, liked songs, and genre suggestions.




Acknowledging SoundCloud's effective inclusion of a "recently played" section, I maintained this feature on the right column along with recommendations of artists based on users' listening history.

Home Page

Addressing the challenge of difficulty in accessing specific playlists from the homepage and the absence of a personalized page, I revamped multiple features across all screens. I made optimal use of available space, as SoundCloud had significant unused white space. Upon entering SoundCloud's mobile app, it was evident that a recent substantial update had been implemented, featuring a new black-and-white logo, replacing the previous orange-and-white one. Additionally, the incorporation of a dark mode, known for reducing eye strain and aligning with design trends, was introduced.

Taking this into consideration:




Search within the playlist and view information such as song title, genre, key, BPM, views, date added, and song duration.




Sort by common genres, keys, BPMs, views, and date added by clicking on one item at a time. This increases efficiency in finding songs that mix well together based on genre, keys, and BPM.




Additionally, a clear display of upcoming songs and recommended songs based on the playlist was implemented for an enhanced user experience.




Playlist Page

Retaining all previous elements such as like, share, copy link, edit, add to next up, and delete, I introduced a more detailed view of user playlists.

This allows users to:




View their recent searches, personalized recommendations from SoundCloud, and explore more categories.




Helps to enhance discovery through both new and existing pathways while ensuring a cohesive user experience.

Search Page

Previously, users faced challenges in searching for songs or artists with exact words, lacking guidance for general discovery. Recognizing that SoundCloud already had more categories hidden on the homepage for discovery, I designed a user-friendly search interface.

Discovering new music can be difficult.

BACKGROUND

SoundCloud stands out as a prominent online audio distribution platform, providing artists with the means to share and promote their music across diverse genres. Specifically tailored for Electronic Dance Music (EDM) and House Music enthusiasts like myself, it offers a valuable space with an extensive collection of tracks, including numerous remixes. Learning how to DJ has emerged as a popular new hobby post-COVID-19, attracting individuals (like me) eager for fresh activities during extended periods at home. Having recently acquired my first DJ controller, I discovered that SoundCloud is one of the best platforms for starting your DJ journey. However, I noticed that it was not as intuitive as it seemed, as, like many people, I faced challenges in pinpointing the right songs for mixing and determining the specific genre I wanted to explore. To gain insights into the experiences of fellow beginner DJs and music enthusiasts, I am eager to explore how others navigate SoundCloud, discover unique remixes, and address similar hurdles in finding suitable tracks for mixing in advance.

User Interviews

RESEARCH

In order to learn more about the SoundCloud experience and identify user needs and paint points. I interviewed three college students that had interests in EDM/House Music and becoming a beginner DJs.

Questions revolved around:




As a beginner in music exploration, how do you go about finding and mixing tracks that align with your preferences (with or without the use of SoundCloud)?




Can you share any challenges you've faced in discovering and selecting music in your chosen genre, and are there any features or tools that have made this process easier or more difficult?




In determining your song choice, what factors influence your decision, and do you seek input or insights from communities or other sources during this exploration?

Key Features that stand out from competitors: Integration with third-party apps, AI DJ, collaborative playlists and blends, seeing friends' activity, yearly wrapped, and exclusive content.

Competitor Analysis

Spotify

RESEARCH

My competitor analysis involves delving into how SoundCloud caters to the needs of beginner DJs and music enthusiasts, specifically by examining user experiences in discovering and mixing tracks. I aim to compare SoundCloud's features and user-friendliness with those of competitors such as Spotify, Apple Music, and Beatport.




⚠️ It's important to note that user preferences may vary, and these pros and cons are based on the general characteristics of each platform. Users may have different experiences based on their specific needs and preferences.

SoundCloud shares features with its competitors, boasting a large library that spans diverse genres and includes numerous remixes. It promotes independent artists and offers accessible features for both DJing and music exploration. However, what sets SoundCloud apart from its competitors is its unique positioning as a perfect middle ground. It bridges the gap between platforms with limited remix libraries and those with expansive collections, making it accessible for rising artists to publish and for users to discover new or remixed music. This distinctive position has led to its adoption by rising artists and music enthusiasts seeking a platform that stands out in the realm of online audio distribution.

Pros

Extensive Music Library: Spotify has a vast collection of tracks across various genres, making it a valuable resource for discovering music.

User-Friendly Interface: Known for its ease of use, Spotify provides a user-friendly interface, which may be beneficial for beginners.

Playlist Recommendations: The platform offers personalized playlist recommendations, helping users discover new tracks tailored to their preferences.

Cons

Remix Availability: While Spotify has a diverse library, it might not have as many remixes as platforms specifically tailored for electronic music.

Key Features that stand out from competitors: Integration with the Apple Ecosystem, exclusive content and early releases, human-curated playlists and radio, and seeing what friends are listening to.

Apple Music

Pros

Wide Music Catalog: Apple Music provides a comprehensive catalog of songs, including a range of genres suitable for different tastes.

Integration with Apple Ecosystem: For users within the Apple ecosystem, the seamless integration with other Apple devices can be an advantage.

Cons

Learning Curve: Some users may find the interface and features of Apple Music to have a steeper learning curve compared to more straightforward platforms.

Key Features that stand out from competitors: Genre-specific focus, DJ-centric features, advanced music discovery tools, integration with DJ software, and exclusive content for events and festivals.

Beatport

Pros

Specialized in Electronic Music: Beatport is known for its focus on electronic dance music (EDM) and house music, providing a curated experience for enthusiasts in these genres.

DJ-Friendly Features: Being a platform targeted at DJs, Beatport offers features that cater to mixing and exploring electronic music.

Cons

Limited Genres: While Beatport excels in electronic music, it may have a more limited selection of tracks outside this genre compared to broader platforms.

1. People feel let down by the personalized and sharing experience




This makes it harder to find music within your playlists or new songs, and also sharing music




When compared to Spotify with Spotify AI DJ, the “blends” with friends, seeing what others listening to, SoundCloud does not have the best personalized and sharing experience

2. Discovering remixes is a challenge for people




With how open SoundCloud is for new artists publishing music, it has it’s pros and cons.




Pros: accessible to anyone to publish, easier process




Cons: makes it harder to create accurate searches, quality of songs are depreciated

3. Artists (Specifically DJs in this case) feel like there is no guidance




One of SoundCloud’s pros is being able to use SoundCloud music in DJ softwares like Rekordbox and Serato, however, as an artist there is no real support in making it a smoother experience from transferring playlists over to seeing what mixes well together to sorting songs.




About SoundCloud:

Identifying Problems

RESEARCH

“One of my favorite songs is ‘So Close’ by NOTD, and when I search it up, I was hoping for more efficient results rather than the search engine thinking I want a different song, like ‘Feel So Close’ by Calvin Harris."

"The results when I search are never the exact thing I’m looking for. The way the results populate makes no sense, as the songs are not organized by most views, most likes, when it was published, or anything, it seems.”

“As someone using SoundCloud as their primary platform for getting music and transferring it over to my DJ software, it is very difficult to confirm if all the songs I added are included, and it’s frustrating when searching for songs with the same BPM if I can’t find the specific song I’m looking for.”

“When I’m trying to listen to music for everyday activities, I can’t search within my playlist, and there is no filter or sorting option to match the vibe I want, so I ultimately switch to my other music platform."

User Pain Points:




People want a more efficient method to discover music tailored to EDM/Pop preferences.

People face difficulty in discovering popular remixes or showcasing work for remix artists.

People desire curated playlists and personalized recommendations for remixes.

After conducting user interviews and competitor analysis, I created an affinity map to identify common pain points among users. The map serves as a guide for redesigning certain issues in SoundCloud, focusing on addressing and improving user experiences based on the insights gathered from both user interviews and competitor analysis.

Affinity Map

RESEARCH

Defining the Problem

After conducting my research, I honed in on a guiding question:




How can we make SoundCloud a more personable experience for users?

Through comprehensive user interviews, competitor analysis, affinity mapping, and pain point identification, I discerned that users primarily focus on three key aspects: accessing existing playlists, discovering new music, and finding tracks suitable for mixing. In response to these insights, I've formulated three redesign goals for SoundCloud:

Developing a Solution

IDEATION

Redesign Goals:




Personalized Homepage: Restructure the homepage to be more personable and aligned with user needs, providing a welcoming and tailored experience upon entry.




Customizable Playlist System: Introduce a sort/filter system for existing playlists, empowering users with a more customizable and efficient playlist management experience.




Enhanced Search Functionality: Develop an improved search system that ensures clarity and avoids user confusion, facilitating a seamless process for discovering new music and tracks for mixing.

With the redesign goals and the synthesis of our comprehensive research, I've crafted a user flow to illustrate the various paths users may take when navigating the screens slated for redesign, highlighting potential scenarios they might encounter along the way.

User Flow

IDEATION

Following the creation of the flow chart, I proceeded to quickly sketch low-fidelity wireframes as a preliminary step to strategize improvements and determine how enhancements can be implemented.

Search Page

After generating low-fidelity sketches, I transitioned to Figma to create the structural design within a MacBook 14-inch frame, aiming to visualize how it would fit on a desktop and making necessary size adjustments.

Mid Fidelity

IDEATION

Final Designs

IDEATION

My redesigns represent an initial stride towards enhancing the SoundCloud experience and addressing the challenges faced by novice DJs and music enthusiasts. Some next steps I would take include:




Additionally, considering the importance of a more personalized experience, I propose the development of an official desktop app. This would not only provide users with a dedicated platform but also contribute to a more seamless and personalized interaction with SoundCloud. Such an initiative aims to enhance user engagement and drive a more substantial user base, ultimately contributing to the platform's growth and popularity.




Conducting another round of interviews and undertaking user testing to evaluate whether my redesign has indeed improved efficiency and effectiveness in music discovery.




Exploring alternative solutions and ensuring a comprehensive redesign that maintains cohesiveness and adheres to a consistent design aesthetic and usability across the entire website.

Next Steps

REFLECTION

Completing this case study within the tight timeframe of 72 hours (Saturday - Monday) presented a significant challenge. However, it showcases my dedication to continuously push my limits as a Product Designer in my ongoing journey of personal discovery and development.




As a novice DJ, exploring the intricacies of SoundCloud was not only educational but also highly enjoyable. It allowed me to find ways to assist individuals like myself in understanding and utilizing the platform more effectively.




In all my projects, I find fulfillment in establishing a personal connection to my work. This connection is shared with others by explaining how I operate, all while ensuring that personal biases do not influence the process. It is my commitment to contributing meaningfully to the field of Product Design while fostering a deeper understanding and connection with users.

Conclusion

REFLECTION

A few things I enjoy when I'm not designing data platforms.

Orchestrating Chaos

I don't just play games. I build worlds. Being a Dungeon Master has become one of my favorite creative outlets.

Drawing Worlds

Illustration is my way of thinking visually. I enjoy drawing stylized characters and imaginary worlds, often inspired by Japanese illustration.

It gives me a space to explore ideas more freely than product design usually allows.

The 1% Improvement

From the fast focus of a table tennis rally to the quiet precision of archery, I enjoy activities that reward patience and practice.

They remind me that meaningful progress rarely comes from dramatic leaps, but from getting a little better every day.

Chief Curiosity Officer

My life has always been shaped by the dogs who share it with me. My late dog Rip taught me a lot about loyalty and companionship.

Today Nova continues that tradition, joining me on hikes, road trips, and small everyday adventures.

Hi, I'm Ruoxuan, but most people call me Nessie. I'm a product designer, currently on contract at Apple, where I work on AI tools for the sales teams.

I care most about the people on the other side of the screen. Before I design anything, I want to know what they're trying to do and what keeps getting in their way. Then I try to make it feel simple, even when there's a lot of data and AI underneath. If someone who isn't an expert can pick it up and enjoy it, I've done my job.

How I started with design.

I came to design through games. By the end of my undergrad, I was sure game design was my future. I wanted to make games that spread happiness to everyone.

Then the pandemic hit, and I shared a game demo with my mom to lift her spirits. It was too hard for her to enjoy, and she asked me if she just wasn't clever enough, if she'd been left behind and could only play games like Candy Crush. That stayed with me. If my own mom couldn't reach the joy I was trying to make, who else was I leaving out?

That's how I found UX. I specialized in it at the University of Texas at Austin, and internships at Sleeper and EchoKids taught me that good design has to work for people and for the business at the same time. Today I bring that to AI products, so they feel easy for anyone to use.

My work history.

I design AI tools for Apple's sales teams, including Predictive Coverage, a map based planning tool with a projected 46% time saved.

I led information architecture and automation design for Leazy, an AI legal platform used by 10+ law firms. Client adoption went up 11%.

Mar 2024 to Aug 2024

May 2022 to Aug 2022

In my spare time.

When I'm not designing, I'm usually gaming. My favorites are Elden Ring, Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, Kirby and the Forgotten Land, and Disco Elysium. The rest of the time goes to my puppy.

pages.text:
Resume
Portfolio
Explorations
I started out my design journey as a cognitive science major at UC Berkeley, driven by my curiosity about human emotion and patterns of decision making.

Along the way, I discovered my passion for designing for adversity and uncertainty. I’m currently exploring design futures and experimenting with emerging technologies as a graduate student at Berkeley MDes. Topics I’ve come into contact with include critical design, the AI-UX intersection, new human-machine interfaces, and designing for mental health.

I have found so much joy in using my skills to strengthen and empower the creative load of the teams I am on and, most importantly, the lives of the individuals I design for. You can reach me at mayachen@berkeley.edu or on LinkedIn.

Most recently a UX Design intern @ Cisco Meraki.
2/2
Storytelling
I use storytelling to heighten my design craft. I believe that emotionally-driven visual and written narratives are extremely powerful devices for communicating product ideas. On any given project, you can expect me to combine film, photography and writing with ethnographic research findings to capture the intangible.
Top to bottom:
Terrascape, Dec 2021 - showing off our interactive dashboard prototype
Veiled Observers, Dec 2021 - an onlooker views our team’s exhibit theme
Soundscript, Oct 2021 - taking my sound capturing machine for a walk in the park
Critical Making
Having grown up in multiple cities and with multiple cultures, I see myself as a global citizen. To me, making is an act that creates ripples across space and time; in light of uncertain (and un-preferred) futures rapidly emerging, I constantly ask myself: what is my responsibility as a designer in a world that’s on a tipping point?

I’ve used my creativity to bring people together during the pandemic, raise awareness of climate change, and make design more accessible. I look forward to continuing this practice in my graduate studies, where I’m working on projects in future-making.
Credit: Unsplash
Human Cognition
I leverage my background in Cognitive Science on my projects, wearing many hats throughout the design process (ethnographer and communicator besides designer). I love thinking through complex and novel problems that are unprecedented in the design space. These days, I’m particularly interested in the connection between design, cognition and computation: my recent projects involve natural language processing and computer vision.

About

Hi, I’m Tushar.

I’m a Senior Product Designer at Microsoft AI, currently working on autonomous agents for the workplace.

I like the stretch between figuring out what to build and making it real. That usually means working closely with engineers, prototyping in code, and paying a lot of attention to what happens when AI gets something wrong.

What I’ve been up to

At Microsoft AI

I work on AI agents for the workplace. I led design for Copilot Cowork and designed Copilot Tasks across web, iOS, and Android. Most of my time goes into making powerful new capabilities feel clear and controllable.

Before that

I spent three years on Microsoft Edge. I led Browser Essentials from zero to 14 million monthly users and worked across Copilot in Edge, tabs, history, and favorites.

On my own time

I design and build products end to end. Fitness Wrapped has more than 70,000 downloads. DyslexiaBuddy, an AI reading coach for children with dyslexia, is used by more than 5,000 families.

How I like to work

I care about getting to the right idea quickly, then working with the team to make it real.

I prototype early.

When an idea depends on timing or model behavior, I build it in code. A working prototype usually answers questions faster than another round of mockups.

I plan for things to go wrong.

AI gets confused and sometimes takes the wrong turn. I make sure people can see what is happening, step in, and recover without losing their work.

I work closely with the team.

I studied computer science before design, so I am comfortable working through the technical details with engineers instead of designing from a distance.

I build tools that save time.

I make prototyping kits and shared playgrounds so other designers can try ideas quickly. If something works for me, I want the rest of the team to have it too.

pages.title: Copilot Cowork – Tushar Gupta
pages.text:
Work
About
Resume
Copilot Cowork

How an early agent prototype became a workspace where people can delegate work, follow its progress, approve actions, and use the result.

My role
Design lead. Set product direction and directly designed the home, sessions, tool approvals, and finished-work experience.
Timeline
Microsoft AI · 2025–now
Outcome
General availability in under three months · Used by more than half of the Fortune 500 during preview
Overview

When I joined the project, Cowork was an early engineering prototype. It could take a request, plan the work, use tools, and produce a result. That proved the underlying agent worked, but the experience still felt like a demo: it was hard to tell what the agent was doing, where to step in, or what you would get back at the end.

My job was to turn that prototype into a product people could use for real work. I led product design as the team created Copilot Cowork: a workspace where you can give an AI agent a multi-step task, follow its progress, answer questions or approve actions, and receive finished work you can open and use.

We had to answer a few basic questions before the product could ship:

How do you know what an agent is doing without watching every step?
When should it stop for approval, and what information do you need to decide?
How do you return to a task later and understand what happened?
How should an hour of agent work be packaged when it is finished?
From prototype to enterprise-ready

I set direction across the design team and worked closely with product, engineering, and research. My direct design work covered the Cowork home, individual work sessions, tool approvals, and the way finished work is presented.

The schedule shaped the approach. Cowork moved from Microsoft’s early-access Frontier program to general availability in under three months. We could not design a different interface for every new capability, so we created a small set of reusable patterns for starting work, tracking it, approving actions, and reviewing results.

Organizing long-running work

The prototype put most of the experience into a chat transcript. That works for a quick answer, but not for a task that runs for an hour or produces several files. We separated the experience into three parts:

Home gives people one place to start a task, see examples, and return to work that is still running.

Sessions keep the original request, plan, current activity, questions, and results together. Instead of searching through messages, you can open the task and see its current state.

A session, start to finish · plan, check-in, tracked steps, finished work

Finished work is presented as a file or deliverable you can open and review, rather than as a long answer buried in the conversation.

Tool approvals as a reusable pattern

Cowork can send email, create calendar events, post in Teams, and use many other tools. Those actions should not happen without a person’s approval. Each approval therefore shows the proposed action, the important details, and why the agent needs permission. From there, the person can approve it, decline it, or tell the agent what to change.

The challenge was scale. Cowork needed this flow for around 120 Microsoft and third-party tools, and each tool has different information. An email needs recipients and a subject; a calendar invite needs a time and attendees; a Teams post needs a channel. Drawing every version by hand in Figma would have been slow to produce and difficult to keep current.

I built a working playground instead. It uses a small set of shared components to render the correct approval for every tool on desktop and mobile. Designers can select a tool and see the real card populated with its data. The playground also exports each scenario as a Markdown specification that engineering’s coding agents can use.

The approval playground · one pattern, 120 tools, desktop and mobile

That approval pattern has since been adopted by other teams across Microsoft.

What shipped
From a Frontier offering to general availability in under three months.
More than half of the Fortune 500 used Cowork during preview.
One of Copilot's highest-retention experiences.
The approval and agent-control patterns spread well beyond the Cowork team.
A coded playground covering around 120 tool approvals across first- and third-party tools, built in place of hand-drawn mocks.

The most useful result was not a single screen. It was a reusable set of patterns for showing what an agent is doing, when it needs a person, and what it produced.

Next project

A clear way to delegate work to Copilot, designed and shipped in eight weeks.

Thanks for dropping by my portfolio! I am currently a 1st-year Master’s student at the University of Washington studying human-centered design. Previously, I studied Digital Media and Art at New York University. 

My design journey began in high school where I designed independent magazines. Since then I have been exploring different mediums to communicate information and build connections with people. This passion led me to pursue a degree in media and art where I learned humanities and digital skills (I 🎨draw, 👩🏻‍💻code, and 💡design) to create works that explore the relationship between people, tech, and society.

Now I’m transitioning into user experience design because I want to create works that are not just fun and aesthetically pleasing, but also MAKE SENSE. After years of exploration, I have found myself to be both a creative and analytical person. While making arts allow my creativity to flourish boundlessly, I enjoyed making sense of information and creating meaningful solutions to address real-world problems. 

MY RESUME
Some recent reflections as a designer:

I used to run out of ideas sometimes as an artist, but now working with people as a designer gives me endless inspiration. YAY!  😆💡

 The city is my homescreen is one of my favorite readings. It talks about how designers should look beyond individual experiences and care for the collective impact. 

Delivery is important. A good idea with a bad delivery could hardly impress people. [Empirical fact: users are more generous if the design is pretty 🌸]

Recently I’ve been:

At school:  learning usability testing and qualitative research methods.

In front of screens: learning design systems, Lens Studio, and motion graphics.

Away from screens: painting with acrylic and markers.

Outdoor:  treasure hunting at Trader Joe’s.

Like my work? Let’s connect!

Born in Atlanta, based in LA. Worn many hats, lived many career chapters. Competitive skateboarder, 911 dispatcher, actor, business founder. Current chapter: building in big tech.

I co-founded Made by Portal, a full-service digital design firm, and bootstrapped it from the ground up—balancing running and scaling the business, securing clients, and delivering high-quality work on tight deadlines, often all at once.

Without venture funding, we had to be agile and resourceful, assembling the right talent, workflow pipelines, and business infrastructure. Our nimble, bespoke model enabled faster delivery and better outcomes through a streamlined talent pipeline.

While we provided a range of design services, our most notable work was in web development, motion graphics & VFX, brand identity, and content strategy, working with both small businesses and larger enterprises.

Over the past decade, I have worked across television, film, advertising, and digital media in a range of creative and strategic roles, from acting in TV & film to production, creative direction, content strategy, research, and advertising. These experiences gave me firsthand insight into audience engagement, storytelling mechanics, and creative execution at scale, perspectives I continue to apply today.

Guiding Principles
Operations

Build the conditions for the work. The ambition has to shape how the work gets done. I build teams, tools, and processes around what the idea requires, and question inherited ways of working when they limit what we can make.

Creative Technology

Work with the material to find the idea. I treat technology as a creative medium. Building in code and experimenting with emerging tools is how I discover possibilities, test assumptions, and let what I learn reshape the direction.

Design

Make the detail accountable to the whole. An interaction can work beautifully on its own and still make the product harder to understand. I move between individual moments and the broader experience, using each to challenge and refine the other.

Storytelling

Use story to make complex ideas resonate. Story establishes what matters, what needs context, and what can fall away. I use it to connect the larger ambition to something people can understand, see themselves in, and act on.

Leadership & Management Approach

Stay close to the work. Make room for others to own it. I’ve led as a founder, a design lead, an educator, and an advisor to executive leadership. Each role calls for a different balance of making, directing, and supporting others. I stay close to the hard parts and make the reasoning behind decisions visible, so people can challenge the thinking and make informed calls of their own. That means knowing when to build alongside someone, offer guidance, or step back and let them lead.

Recognition & Awards

My work has been recognized by leading industry organizations and design platforms, highlighting a focus on innovation, impact, and craftsmanship across disciplines.

LAUNCHED
LumonOS

A 36-hour AI sprint to build Lumon Industries’ OS from Severance.

Overview

Had an idea at lunch on Saturday: What if I built Lumon Industries’ OS from Severance as a real web app? (Apple/Ben Stiller, please don’t sue me. Made with ❤️, as a fan, for educational purposes!)

In a focused 36-hour sprint, I designed and developed an interactive web experience, closely matching screens from the show while inventing additional interfaces to deliver a complete end-to-end flow. I also integrated a GPT-4o-powered "LumonAI" chat tuned to Kier’s voice, and produced a concise sizzle video showcasing the entire journey.

App FYIs:

➡️ Chat interactions are limited to 3 questions per session to manage API costs.

➡️ Credentials are stored temporarily in a session cookie and auto-delete afterward.

➡️ The experience is optimized for desktop but fully functional on mobile.

This quick-turn experiment highlights the future of creative work, leveraging AI to amplify productivity, accelerate innovation, and rapidly transform bold ideas into tangible outcomes.

FAQ's
Why did I use AI?

Folks who know me know I'm bullish on emerging tech—AI now fuels about 90% of my workflow. Honestly can't remember the last time I didn't use some AI-powered tool.

Reality check: Sure, I can design, code, and make videos. But integrating AI has easily 10x’d (or more) my output. I'm fast—but not that fast.

As I always tell my design students: don’t restrict yourself. Build your skillset like a Swiss Army knife—pulling out the right tool for each job. AI makes blending disciplines even easier, shifting us from specialists into creative technologists and multi-faceted builders. No single tool or workflow should limit your expression or approach to problem-solving.

➡️ The broader your toolkit, the richer your work.
‍
➡️ Experiment often (the best ideas happen here), and just make more things.
‍
➡️ Show more, say less.
‍
➡️ Learn and share openly, grow together.


What tech did I use?

➡️ App Tech Stack: Nextjs, GSAP, Vercel, GitHub, OpenAI GPT4o (Lumon AI chat), VercelAISDK (streaming & tool calling).

➡️ Regular Tools Used: Figma, Illustrator, AfterEffects, Cursor, hashtag#Terminal.

➡️ AI Tools Used: Cursor Chat claude, ChatGPT (text/images), Sora (video gen), KlingAI (video gen).

‍

Credits

➡️ Inspiration: Severance episodes (screenshots), YouTube, shout out to Jono Yuen for your HUD/GUI website, great reference for what UI was used in the show. Original Login UI forked and remixed from https://lnkd.in/eYuteyXE

➡️ Music used: https://lnkd.in/gSPtPuUh

PORTFOLIO

CONTACT

Portfolio

Below is a small sample of my work please click on any projects you find interesting to read more about them. Specific information always available on request.

Design System Philips

Global Experience Director

As Philips is moving towards a future-proof, solution-based company this meant a change to processes and models of work that support design and development at scale. A living resource of principles, guidelines, best practices and toolkits to help Philips design and build consistent, scalable yet flexible propositions across the health continuum was created. 

Go to Project
Swisscard | Contact Center Redesign

Director | Customer Strategy & Design

This project enhanced the call center experience for both agents and customers. The project gathered feedback from both agents and customers through surveys, interviews & workshops to understand their needs and expectations. Based on the feedback, the end goal was to create a more efficient and satisfying experience, resulting in increased customer satisfaction and improved agent morale.

Go to project
Gulf Bank | Redesign

Lead & Principle UX

This was a redesign project for Gulf Bank, a leading financial institution in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region. Gulf Bank had been facing a number of challenges that affected its brand perception and customer experience, including an outdated visual identity, inconsistent communication, and a complex user interface for its digital channels.

In response, the bank engaged myself and a small  team of designers and consultants to develop a comprehensive redesign strategy that would address these issues and position Gulf Bank as a modern, innovative, and customer-centric financial brand. 

Go to project
Conversational AI | Ally Assist

Global Experience Director

In today's fast-paced world, sleep has become an increasingly rare and precious commodity. Poor sleep can have a significant impact on both physical and mental health, leading to decreased productivity, mood swings, and a host of other issues. To address this problem, Philips tasked my team with creating a mobile app that will help people actively engage with and improve their sleep. Our app will provide users with the tools and resources via a conversational AI to help track their sleep patterns, set goals, and make lifestyle changes that can promote better sleep hygiene. By leveraging the latest technology and cutting-edge research in sleep science, our app empowers users to take control of their sleep.

Go to project
Cloud9 IDE

Senior UX Designer

Cloud9 IDE is an online development environment for Javascript and Node.js applications as well as HTML, CSS, PHP, Java, Ruby and 23 other languages. As 1 of 2 designers in this start-up we created the worlds first online development environment. It allows developers to write, run, and debug their code together in real time with this powerful and flexible tool. Developers can collaborate on their projects publicly, or keep them private. Company exited with a sale to Amazon where it is still part of their AWS developer tool set. 

Go to project
Learn Between

Head of Design

Learn Between is a mobile application designed to empower individuals by providing them with valuable knowledge and skills in easily digestible 15-minute sessions, thoughtfully scheduled and seamlessly integrated into their calendars. Time is a precious resource, and carving out dedicated learning periods can be a challenge in our hectic lives. That's why the app leverages the power of artificial intelligence to optimize learning experiences and make education more accessible, flexible, and engaging than ever before. The philosophy behind Learn Between is to break down complex subjects into bite-sized, manageable lessons that can be effortlessly absorbed during short intervals.

Go to project

pages.title: Jason Cho — Visual Designer
pages.text:
Jason Cho
jason@jasoncho.ca
Messages

Messages by Google is the most popular app for texting (SMS, MMS) and chat (RCS) on Android. From defining the design system to setting a high bar for implementation, I oversee the visual design of Messages with the mission of making our app shine ✨

Recorder

With Creative Lab, we designed and launched Recorder — Google’s first audio recording app with on-device machine learning. Recorder is featured on Google Design's Best of 2019.

Clock & Calculator

In 2019, I led the UX for Android Clock and Calculator by defining UX vision, refreshing the visual layout and collaborating with teams across Google to integrate a suite of features including Bedtime.

About

I'm a visual designer at Google working on Messages. Born in Seoul, raised in Vancouver, I'm currently designing exciting messaging features in Mountain View, CA. Above all, my life goal is to follow the words of 1 John 4:7.

As I navigate the world of design and engineering, I've found inspiration a long time ago while traveling through Kanto with Raichu and trying to reproduce the New York skyline while sketching the iconic Spider-Man. Like a burst of yellow against the dark, my journey has taken me through cities and electrical networks, shaping my perspective.

Design is a craft, and studying the method behind the methods is what drives me. I've learned that listening is the gateway to understanding, and understanding is the first step toward solving any problem. I try to work both hard and smart, not lose myself in the process. Loved ones, mentors, peers, partners, and obviously, users, anchor me in reality.

I'm on a mission to craft interfaces, products, and systems for the software makers, the details lovers, and the efficiency maestros. I dedicate my work to empowering teams, understanding that methods and tools can be transformative forces in amplifying their efforts to achieve the extraordinary. I'm committed to reshaping how people work, ensuring they can reach new heights and turn the impossible into reality.

This personal space reflects my journey as a designer, engineer, and maker. Through experiences and self-reflection, I've evolved and established guiding principles that are the bedrock of all my collaborations and projects. These principles are unwavering guides in my ongoing pursuit of mastering my craft.

This is my playground, a non-portfolio-only digital place where I share my thoughts, experiments and projects I'm working on. Welcome to Thunderstorm.

ABOUT

I design and build 0→1 AI products, end to end.

AI product designer and design engineer based in the San Francisco Bay Area — working across product design, front-end engineering, and product architecture.

HELLO

I’m Yichen, an AI product designer and design engineer. I work end-to-end — from the first sketch to shipped code — most often on 0→1 AI products.

Lately that has meant building things like dim.app, invoko.ai, and StayPass: designing the experience, then shipping it directly in code with agentic workflows. I care about restraint and craft. I don’t just design for how things feel and look, but also how they work.

Before going independent I spent three and half years at Microsoft on Windows + Devices, prototyping AI and OS experiences. I studied Interaction Design (B.Des) at the University of Washington.

Designer, mom of 2 and more

Hello, I’m Kaiting Huang, a multidisciplinary product designer with 10+ years of experience in big tech and startups. Currently based in Seattle, WA, and focused on design with Gen AI.

Born and raised in Taiwan, I majored in Business in college but realized that compared to promoting products, I like designing products even better. The thought made me embark on a decade-long journey spanning across Europe and the U.S. where I gained knowledge and experiences in design, tech, and human behaviors. 

In my professional career, I have worked on planet-scale consumer experiences as well as highly customized enterprise solutions. I appreciate designs that demonstrate simplicity, clarity, and profoundness.

My passion lies in creating things. Other than designing tech products, I also like playing piano and guitar, tackling home DIY projects, and finding creative ways to connect with my twin kids.

Buzz Usborne
Menu
Hej!

I’m Buzz ✌🏼 a British/Australian dad, designer and creativity enthusiast working just outside Sydney, Australia 🇦🇺. I love producing high quality, creative solutions to problems that don’t have obvious answers.

It’s me. That’s a sign of love 🖕

I’m most interested in creating the conditions for design quality at scale. I’m the person who sits between ambitious ideas, emerging technology and difficult customer problems — and the bridge between those and our ability to execute. I make ideas sharper, more original and more useful. I turn complexity into clarity, find ideas their unique opinion and help teams ship work they didn’t think they were capable of.

I go where the work needs me — from writing code to writing strategy, from teaching and building AI-native design processes, to helping exceptional teams do their best creative work.

I’m happiest in ambiguity and high stakes, turning half-formed ideas into memorable customer experiences. The bigger and more unknown the problem, the better. I’m not precious about the medium, software or technique — I care about finding the core of an idea, then working with designers, engineers and product teams to make it exceptional.

I’ve proudly mixed player/coach as Principal Designer at Help Scout and Atlassian… as Design Director at Campaign Monitor and Buildkite, Head of Product at Sendle and Lead Designer at Skype and various agencies around the world.

I also founded Prevue, a design presentation product used by more than 40,000 agencies worldwide to share millions of concepts and gather client feedback. I built and ran Prevue solo for over a decade until its acquisition in 2018. Along the way, I taught myself to code, deepened my visual design craft and learned how to turn design judgement into a real, profitable business.

Computers are cool, but…

I spend a lot of time offline, too. I find people, processes and the systems we use to communicate fascinating. Before design, I was a competitive sailor and coach — teaching people of all ages and abilities while competing in internationally recognised events. I worked as an ⛵ Olympic sailing coach and lived in the Mediterranean for a while before realising it might be time to point myself toward software.

My mind is never too far from the ocean. When I’m not online, you’ll usually find me outside with my wife and kids — travelling, swimming, sand-running or generally trying to remember that the best ideas rarely arrive while staring at a screen.

I’m always up for a virtual coffee and a chat — just drop me a line and we’ll set something up. Alternatively if you email, I promise I’ll reply.

pages.title: Buzz Usborne • Help Scout Inbox
pages.text:
Buzz Usborne
Menu
Inbox
SUMMARY

Help Scout is a customer service platform trusted by businesses around the world to deliver delight to hundreds of thousands of customers every day. It’s made up of chat, AI and embeddable products — with an shared Inbox at its core.

I’m pretty sure I confidently declared “email is dead” when I worked at Skype 17 years ago! How wrong I was. Email remains the lifeblood of companies that understand the deep value of delightful, human, and context-rich customer support — and that’s where Help Scout comes in.

But it’s not just email anymore. AI supplements context. Real-time chat and social channels complement long-form threads. Even how we communicate has evolved — with emoji, team collaboration, and integrations expanding our ability to delight. One thing’s clear… how we email today is very different from all those years ago.

This was the challenge I faced at Help Scout: preparing our core experience for the future. The shared inbox, once industry-leading, was now a 12-year-old product straining under technical limitations and growing expectations. It was time to reimagine it from the ground up — a project that took me a year of design, testing and constant iteration.

Before & after. Visually similar, fundamentally different.

Good bones 🦴
Direct link

Every decision was grounded in three core principles: to enable world-class support, to offer deep personalization for every user, and to surface the rich context needed to deliver truly delightful experiences.

One of the biggest challenges — and ultimately, one of the greatest rewards — was designing an interface flexible enough to support deep customization in both layout and behavior. From wide-screen views and collapsing sidebars to formatting toolbars and quick menus, Inbox adapts to the unique role and workflow of each individual.

Another fun (and surprisingly complex) challenge was designing for a wide range of content types while maintaining clarity and legibility within a dense interface. One solution was leveraging AI to detect and truncate non-original content — helping keep every email focused, scannable, and easy to read.

Make writing fun!
Direct link

Designing an editor is no joke. There’s how it resizes with content, how formatting tools behave, how add-ons are integrated — and that’s before you even get to the different modes: notes, drafts, forwards, edits. It’s a surprisingly complex ecosystem.

But because writing is at the heart of great support, it was absolutely worth the effort. After 50+ iterations, deep research, and hundreds of prototypes, we landed on a design that’s simple, focused, and puts content first. It’s an experience built for accessibility, optimized for legibility, and ready to scale with the growing demands of AI-powered support.

Attention to detail ✨
Direct link

Spending your day replying to emails can be a drag, so I looked for every opportunity to add moments of fun, personality, and humanity. Bright colors, rounded corners, and a playful tone of voice helped turn the inbox into a space where magic happens.

Read: Behind the Scenes
I wrote about how we reimagined Inbox — why it needed a fresh start, and how we navigated thousands of pieces of feedback to get it right.

Psst… wanna see something fun? I’ve always believed AI should help people create magic — not replace them. So I designed a t-shirt that celebrates the squishiness and uniqueness of human-first support:

🖕🏼 It's me.

What I wanted to show you…
I love bringing complex, business-critical projects to life — without losing sight of soul, fun, or creative opinion. Even at scale, I believe the little “just because” details still matter.
What I learned…
This product impacted hundreds of thousands of customers, and I spent countless hours personally responding to their frustration. One of the biggest takeaways was learning how to balance resistance to change with genuine pain points, and reacting accordingly.
